planting.note: Plant container-grown shrubs in spring in sheltered, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, out of cold winter wind; this Himalayan species is noticeably less cold-hardy than the common garden paperbush and needs a protected microclimate at the cool edge of its range.

directions: Native to montane forests of Nepal, Bhutan, and southwestern China, this larger, less cold-hardy relative of the familiar Edgeworthia chrysantha grows into a substantial multi-stemmed shrub with the same flexible, knot-able bark once used for traditional Himalayan Lokta paper. In late winter it opens dense, drooping, tubular yellow flower clusters thickly coated in silvery-white silky hairs, fragrant and showy against bare branches before the lance-shaped leaves emerge. Because it comes from higher, cooler Himalayan slopes rather than lowland Japan or China, it tolerates somewhat more cold than other subtropical paperbushes but still demands a sheltered site shielded from drying winter wind and hard freezes. Give it consistently moist, fertile, acidic to neutral soil and dappled shade, and avoid pruning after midsummer so next winter's flower buds are not removed.
